title: The Season's First Wall
summary: The season has opened its account on the Glassroad: a wall is standing up north of the span and walking south along the canyon like it owns the tolls. Shrine-Keeper Toll has finally agreed — thirty-one years late — to evacuate his library, but not, he wishes it recorded, himself. Collect the wrapped books from the mid-span shrine, then run the face down to the temple steps before it files the whole road under weather.

objectives.label: Make the south gate before the road closes
Take Toll's wrapped library aboard at the mid-span shrine
Outrun the wall down the span to the temple-steps shelter

offer.text: Kid. That first wall was a warning shot off the spine. This one's the season properly opening its account — and it's standing up *on the road*, north end, walking south like it bought tickets.
Toll has finally agreed to evacuate. His books, I mean. The man himself is staying welded to the mid-span 'in case the echo needs a witness'. His words. He had them notarised.

Courier. The library is wrapped — forty-one travellers, tarred paper, string in the Guild knot Devanna taught me. Take them to the temple steps where the quiet is thick. The canyon says hurry. It has never once said hurry.
So: fetch a bookshop off a collapsing deadline and then race a mountain down a canyon. Sure. The library card better be transferable.

accept.text: South gate, mid-span, straight down the throat to the temple steps. The Choir's holding the shelter open — Cantor's orders, and for once the whole desert agrees with a Cantor's orders.
Kest, survey camp. Wall's holding twenty-nine metres per second and *organised*, Varga. There's a shape in the front like handwriting. Noted. Not dwelt on. Nineteen minutes to the gate. Go.
The temple steps are swept and the door stands open, courier. Lamps too — not that you'll see them, mid-weather, but a door that expects you is measurably warmer. We measured.
Copy all. Nineteen minutes, one librarian's life work, zero stopping. If Toll asks, his shrine said goodbye back.

complete.text: The travellers arrived? All forty-one? Good. Good. The wall went over the shrine an hour ago, and the echo came back with sand in it, and it is *still finishing the sentences*, courier. It learned to finish them anyway. I may never leave that span.

Pem on band nine. The wall recited the whole way down the canyon, station — not words, the *shape* of words, like a mouth practicing in private. Something is rehearsing. Doors open for things that rehearse.
You carried paper through a storm that was trying to read it. The Choir owes the Driftline a shelter, held open, any season, no toll. We hear you, Ash Varga. Increasingly, so does everything else.

Shelter logged, books dry, rider dusty. That's the road closed until the season says otherwise, kid — the map just got smaller, and everything we still have to do is on the far side of the weather. Rest the bike. Charge the cells. It's going to be that kind of year.
